posts.text: As you may be sick of hearing from me already on this blog, I think the Cop31 theme tune “Let’s Cop” is a bit of a catchy banger. “Bring down the heat make it drop.” “One world, one call, let’s Cop.” But there may be a cruel twist that might quell my enthusiasm. First, have a listen. One of my Australian reporter…

We’ve now heard from Shavkat Mirziyoyev, from Uzbekistan, who has described safeguarding our planet as “a sacred responsibility we all share”. He was followed by an unscheduled intervention from a representative from Azerbaijan, the host of Cop29, who highlighted some of the achievements from the climate summit in…

Nazar Mohammed Saeed Amedi, president of Iraq, is citing the country’s past as Mesopotamia, “the cradle of human civilisation” and one of the first birthplaces of agriculture, and contrasting it with the challenges that climate change is already bringing it. He says the loss of arable land and projected hit to water…

We’re now hearing from Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov, leader of Turkmenistan. He’s speaking about efforts to modernise his country’s energy infrastructure and calling for greater climate resilience in the face of worsening weather. Turkmenistan is an oil and gas producer that has become infamous for its vast emissions of…

The first national leader to speak is Mohamed Cheikh El Ghazouani, President of Mauritania, who is calling for an increase in the assistance given to countries most affected by climate change. “Despite the limited carbon footprint it has, Mauritiania has been suffering greatly from climate change and its consequences,…

Murat Kurum, Turkey’s climate minister and Cop31 president, is now up. He’s detailing the weather extremes battering countries around the world, while making the case for how climate action is in countries’ national interests – by boosting energy security, for instance. He’s making some similar points to Bowen on the…

Chris Bowen, Australia’s climate minister and president of the negotiations, is framing the talks as a challenge for multilaterism in the face of threats from worsening weather to geopolitics. “It’s no exaggeration to say the world is facing a polycrisis – not challenges on one front, but on multiple fronts, all at…

Celeste Saulo, secretary-general of the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), is sweeping through the scientific findings that underpin everything that is being discussed in Antalya. CO2 in the atmosphere is 50% higher than in the preindustrial era. Land and oceans cannot keep up. The Earth energy imbalance is at…

The President of the UN general assembly, Khalilur Rahman, has just opened the segment for heads of state and government. He’s making a plea for action and multilaterism before leaders of dozens of nations make their contributions – with a reminder about what really matters. “Speeches do not cool our planet. Decisions…

The national security of all countries is at risk from the climate crisis, as “science fiction” scenarios of widespread destruction are already coming true and economic shocks from fossil fuels are now the norm rather than the exception, the UK’s foreign secretary is to warn world leaders gathered in Turkey. Ed…

‘I am no longer satisfied with promises’ This week I’ve been speaking to young climate activists at Cop31. Today I spoke to Sohanur Rahman, 29, from Bangladesh, who survived a super-cyclone as a child. He became a key figure in the fight against climate change in Bangladesh after founding YouthNet for Climate Justice…

UK heatwaves could cost London more than £25bn in lost productivity over the next decade, the mayor of London will tell world leaders. Through analysis from City Hall, which also estimates the 2026 heatwaves cost the capital about £2.5bn in lost productivity, Sadiq Khan will underline the economic consequences of…

Erdogan has moved on to the “genocide and ecocide” that he says is happening in Gaza, and his comments are finding some applause. And now he returns to his ecological theme from earlier. “Enough of the greedy mindset that sacrifices ecology for economy.” “May God guide or path and good fortune.” He wishes Ethiopia,…

Erdogan spends some time thanking people and explaining how the rooms at the venue are named after legendary Turkish figures before launching into an almost Deep Ecology-style lament. “As humanity we only have one roof over our home, namely the sky, as humanity we only have one garden, namely the Earth,” he said. “Let…
